region.text: the whole Sudan with Darfur (modern Sudan and South Sudan)

events.note: Darfur is Anglo-Egyptian Sudan's from 1916-17: 'the British conquered Darfur in 1916 and Dinar was killed in battle'; 'The kingdom was incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Condominium in 1917.' The anglo-egyptian-sudan_1916 keyframe that should have carried it does not resolve (the gazetteer has no 'Sarra Triangle'), so the draft keeps Darfur (about 1,086 cells) under british-africa until the 1934 keyframe snap; this event gives it to the Sudan from 1 January 1930, the first year of this window.

region.text: Rehe (Jehol) Province and the land around it that Cliopatria draws as Manchukuo's from 1932, beyond Manchukuo's 1932 shape

events.note: 4 March 1933: 'Rehe was subsequently annexed to Manchukuo' (infobox date 4 March 1933). The page names Chaoyang and Kailu (25 February), Chifeng (after fighting from 2 March) and Chengde (4 March) among the places taken, more than the 160 km Chengde circle the Manchukuo dossier uses (about 320 cells); the rest of the province (about 700 cells) stays land nobody holds in the draft from 1932 until Mengjiang in 1936. The region is Cliopatria's Japanese shape of 1932-35 in Inner Mongolia, Hebei, Beijing and Tianjin, less what Manchukuo's 1932 shape already holds. The region also takes in a western strip of Chahar near Duolun (about 200 cells, the land Mengjiang's 1936 founding takes) and is larger than the province's infobox area (179,982 km2, Rehe Province page): for that strip, the Mengjiang page says 'In a series of actions, starting in 1933, the armies of Manchukuo and Japan occupied Chahar and in 1936 proclaimed itself the independent Mongol Military Government' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mengjiang).

region.text: the Dominion's island and Labrador inside the line of the Privy Council's 1927 decision (the modern province's outline); the gain takes only the cells Canada holds there

events.note: Companion of keyframe_overrides/1 (canada_1932), added by the reviewer: 10 border cells of Labrador inside the 1927 line (near the Strait of Belle Isle and on the Torngat watershed) were Canada's in the 1930 anchor, and the override, which takes Newfoundland and Labrador out of Canada's 1932 shape, would leave them unowned from 1932. 'On 1 March 1927, the Judicial Committee issued a decision that sided with Newfoundland's interpretation of the border'; the 1949 Newfoundland Act's territory is 'the Coast of Labrador as delimited in the report delivered by the Judicial Committee'. So the land is the Dominion's from 1927; this event gives it back from 1 January 1930, the first year of this window (1927-1929 lie in p1920-p1929).

region.text: Western Ukraine: Eastern Galicia and Volhynia (the Lviv, Ivano-Frankivsk, Ternopil, Volyn and Rivne lands), the Polish land the Union already holds

events.note: November 1939: the annexed Polish lands of Western Ukraine are appended to the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic. Soviet invasion of Poland page: 'In November 1939 the Soviet government annexed the entire Polish territory under its control' and 'The Soviet Union appended the annexed territories to the Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republics'. The compile gave the eastern Polish land to the Union direct in September (union ledger/12, second-polish-republic ledger/33), so the republic's own gain from Poland (ledger/32) found only 5 cells; this gain from the Union hands Western Ukraine (about 340 cells) to the republic in the month the page gives. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

region.text: Kyrgyzstan, the Kirghiz SSR of 1936-1991: the Union-held cells inside it

events.note: 1937: the Kirghiz SSR, a union republic since 5 December 1936, holds its whole land. Kirghiz SSR page: 'On 5 December 1936, with the adoption of the 1936 Soviet Constitution, it became a separate constituent republic of the USSR'. Sixty-six cells of Kyrgyzstan stood as Union-direct land inside the republic: 43 taken by the year-end snap of the Union's 1926 shape (window p1920-p1929) and 23 taken from China by the snap of its 1936 shape, which sits at the end of the year and so cannot be followed by an event of 1936. Bridging: January 1937 is the first month the compile can hand them to the republic. Confidence 2: the page dates the republic, not the cells. Companion of p1960-p1969 events/7. (Seam round sm-07, 2 Nov 2026.)

correction.text: unchanged shape, but it holds for 1932-1934 only: the Jiangxi Soviet is abandoned from October 1934 and Ruijin falls in November 1934 (10 November, infobox); the Eyuwan bases in Henan, Hubei and Anhui go in November 1934; the Sichuan-Shaanxi base is left in March 1935; the Zhejiang, Guangdong, Hunan and Guizhou soviets are gone by 1935 (ledger). The same shape is used for 1931

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's correction says this shape 'holds for 1932-1934 only' but leaves from/to empty, so it runs to the end of Cliopatria's span (1935) and, with the 1935 keyframe, the compiler draws the old Jiangxi, Hubei and Sichuan-Shaanxi soviets (about 1,100 cells) through 1935. 'on 10 October 1934 the CCP decided to abandon its Jiangxi Soviet and headquarters in Ruijin' and 'Finally, in October 1935, Mao's army reached Shaanxi province and joined with local Communist forces there'; this entry ends the scattered-soviets shape in 1934 so that 1935 is the northern-Shaanxi keyframe alone.

minus.text: Newfoundland and Labrador, a Dominion of its own until 1949

correction.text: Cliopatria's Canada of 1932-48 without the land of Newfoundland and Labrador

keyframe_overrides.why: The shape (129 cells inside the modern province, 119 of them taken from the Dominion of Newfoundland by the 1932 snap, in south-western Labrador) overlaps the Dominion's Labrador. 'On 1 March 1927, the Judicial Committee issued a decision that sided with Newfoundland's interpretation of the border'; the page describes no Canadian or Quebec administration of Labrador between 1927 and 1949, when the Newfoundland Act defined the province to include 'the Coast of Labrador as delimited in the report' of the 1927 ruling.

union.text: Rehe (Jehol) Province and the land around it that Cliopatria draws as Manchukuo's from 1932, beyond Manchukuo's 1932 shape

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 1932 without Tibet's land, which the Republic claimed but did not govern: 'Since 1912, Tibet had been de facto independent of Chinese control'; with Rehe (Jehol) Province and the land around it, which stays Chinese until the Japanese offensive of February-March 1933

keyframe_overrides.why: The shape leaves Rehe out from 1932 (Cliopatria draws it as Manchukuo's) and the compiler turns the gap (about 1,000 cells) into land nobody holds until 1933 and, west of Chengde, until 1936. The page says Japan captured Rehe 'from the Chinese warlord Zhang Xueliang': 'On February 23, 1933, the offensive was launched', Chaoyang and Kailu fell on 25 February, Chifeng from 2 March, 'On March 4 Japanese cavalry and the 1st Special Tank Company with Type 89 tanks took Chengde, the capital of Rehe'. So Rehe is the Republic's at the end of 1932; events/1 gives it to Manchukuo in March 1933.
